The Petitioners No.1 to 3 have filed this petition against Respondents under Sec.166 of Motors Vehicles Act, 1989 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of case is as under:
Petitioner No.1 is the mother, petitioner No.2 is father, petitioner No.3 is sister of the deceased Vineeth K. SCCH 5 That on 26.01.2022 at about 01.04 a.m. said Vineeth K.
had been going near Windsor Mannere Bridge, T.Chowdaiah Road, Bengaluru on his motor cycle bearing Reg.No.TN09CP2349 slowly and cautiously, a Goods Container Lorry bearing Reg.No.NL01K9803 rash and negligently entered the Smt. sentences.text:
side road of Windsor Mannere Brdge which is purely meant of two wheeler & LMV not for heavy goods vehicle, ignoring guidelines, the driver of the said lorry entered this road without observing height barrier girder erected in the middle of the road and without giving any indications to the road users on back side, so that, motor cycle of the deceased dashed against the said lorry during night hours and caused accident,
due to the force of impact, deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body, hence he SCCH 5 was taken to Mallige Hospital, thereafter taken to Abhaya Hospital, Hosur Road, Bengaluru, wherein taken treatment as indoor patient for 10 days, but ultimately succumbed to the accidental injuries on 04.02.2022.
Petitioners have taken the dead body to their home and performed funeral ceremony by way of spending an amount of Rs.10,00,000/ including medical expenses.

3. At the time of accident, Vineeth K. was aged about 24 years, hale and healthy, he was working as GSAF & B Service at Sheraton Grand, Bangalore Hotel at Brigade Gateway, Bengaluru, thereby earning Rs.20,000/ p.m. and contributing his entire income towards needs and welfare of the petitioners, except his income, petitioners had no means of income, due to the sad demise of Vineeth, petitioners have lost their bread, SCCH 5 further they have lost their love and affection.
Out of this accident crime No.01/2022 is registered against the said lorry and its driver before the High Grounds Traffic Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337, 304(A) of IPC.
R1 is the owner, R2 is insurer of the said lorry, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.70,00,000/ with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
4.
On service of notice, R1/owner has not appeared, hence placed exparte.

R2/insurer has appeared before the court and filed written statement denying entire case of the petitioners, further stated that, he is entitled to take shelter under Sec.147 and 149 of M.V.Act, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) of M.V.Act, SCCH 5 petitioners have to prove the negligency of the lorry driver, it is only involvement of the said lorry by colluding with the police, further he is liable to indemnify the R1, if R1 has complied the policy conditions, further rider of the motor cycle had no driving license at the time of accident, there is negligency of the motor cyclist, claim made by the petitioners is higher side, hence petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On going through the rival pleadings, this tribunal has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1.Whether Petitioners prove that, deceased Late.Vineeth K. died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 26.01.2022 at about 01.04 a.m. when deceased was riding his motor SCCH 5 cycle bearing Reg.No.TN09CP2349 near Windsor Mannor Bridge, T.Chowdaiah Road, Bengaluru, at that time, Lorry bearing Reg.No.NL01 K9803 driven by its driver in a rash and negligently dashed against the deceased, as mentioned in claim petition?
Smt. Vimala K vs Ms Glovis India Pvt. Ltd on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38419745/
3 2.
Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What order or award?
6.
In order to prove their case, petitioner No.2 has deposed his evidence as PW1, examined one witness as PW2 and marked 24 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.43 and closed their evidence.

On the other hand, inspite of granting sufficient time, R2 has not appeared and deposed his evidence,
lastly his evidence is taken as nil.
SCCH 5 7.

Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:

As per the story of the petitioners, they are parents and sister of the deceased Vineeth K., said Vineeth K. was aged about 24 years, working at Sheraton Grand Bangalore Hotel at Brigade Gateway, Bengaluru, thereby earning Rs.20,000/ p.m., contributing his income to the family.

That on 26.01.2022 at about 01.04 a.m. due to negligency of the SCCH 5 driver of the lorry bearing Reg.No.NL01K9803, this accident is caused near Windsor Mannere Bridge,
T.Chowdaiah Road, Bengaluru, hence they are entitled for compensation of Rs.70,00,000/ from R1 and R2.
9.
In the case on hand, R1/owner has not appeared and contested the petition.
R2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement, but not deposed his evidence.
In his written statement taken contention that, there is no negligency of driver of the lorry, but he has not chosen to examine the driver of the lorry.
Further he has not given his evidence.

10. On going through the police papers it is noticed that, copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of panchanama is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.4, SCCH 5 copy of Sec.133 Notice is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of reply notice is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of MLC extract is marked as Ex.P.7, copy of inquest is marked as Ex.P.8, copy of P.M.
Report is marked as Ex.P.9, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.10.

On going through the said documents it reveals that, very accident is occurred on 26.01.2022 at about 01.04 a.m. near Windsor Mannor Bridge, T.Chowdaish Road, Bengaluru, this accident is occurred due to parking of the heavy goods vehicle in prohibited area, it is noticed that during night hours lorry driver has driven his lorry and struck down in narrow road without observing above fixed grills nearby bridge, meantime this deceased/motor cyclist has come and dashed on back side of the lorry, sustained multiple grievous injuries.
SCCH 5
Petitioners have made efforts to save him with good medical aid in Mallige Hospital and Abhaya Hospital, but ultimately he succumbed to the injuries out of this accident.

12. Further after investigation, Investigation Officer has filed charge sheet only against the lorry driver for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 304(A) of IPC, further for the offences punishable under Sec.115 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules and under Sec.190(2) of Indian Motor Vehicle Act 1988 it goes to show that there is negligency on the part of lorry driver.
However, motor cyclist dashed on back side of the lorry and lorry was struck under the iron grid.
The deceased would have avoided the accident, if he would have moved his motor cycle slowly, but he has not taken such care and driven SCCH 5 the motor cycle in high speed

, impact and result of the accident speaks that,
motor cyclist was in high speed at the time of accident.
13. To elicit the said facts and defend his case, R1/owner would have appeared before this court and contested the petition, but he has not chosen to appear and contest the petition.

R2/insurer has appeared and filed objections, crossexamined the PW1, but not deposed his evidence with any such defence, there is no eyewitness in this case, but after investigation, charge sheet is filed against the driver of the lorry.
The involvement of the vehicles is not disputed, place, date and time of the accident is not disputed.

Under such circumstances, in the absence of defence evidence this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, very accident is SCCH 5 occurred due to negligency of the lorry driver and there is no contributory negligence of the motor cyclist.
With these views I have answered the above issue No.1 in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:
As per the case of the petitioners, deceased Vineeth K. was aged about 24 years at the time of accident.

In this regard they have produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.18,
accordingly he is born in the year 1998, the very accident is occurred on 09.06.2022, relying on Ex.P.18 age of the deceased is considered as 24 years at the time of his death and multiplier 18 is applicable with reference to Sarla Verma case.
15. As per the case of the petitioners, deceased was working as GSAF & B Service at Sheraton Grand SCCH 5 Bangalore Hotel at Brigade Gateway, Bengaluru, thereby earning Rs.20,000/ p.m.

To prove his nature of the work, they have produced copy of Sheraton Hotel Employee ID Card marked as Ex.P.16, copy of Hotel Management Certificate marked as Ex.P.17, but they have not produced any documents regarding income of the deceased.

Under such circumstances, in the absence of considerable evidence about nature of the work and income, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the deceased is taken at the rate of Rs.15,500/ p.m.

As per the case of Sarla Varma, if the deceased is bachelor, then 1/2 of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so that, 1/2 of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.

Petitioners are also entitled for medical expenses of Rs.33,040/, for which they have produced medical bills marked as Ex.P.12, clinical report marked as Ex.P.13.

with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount,
23.

In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.
SCCH 5 71290031210100000279, which is valid for the period from 23.04.2021 to 22.04.2022, the alleged accident was occurred on 26.01.2022, it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Further driver of the Goods Container Lorry by name T.Rukmangathan had driving licence at the time of the accident, copy of the same is on record, hence naturally liability of R1 shall go against R2, so that, R2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:

Inview of the above reasoning and discussions to the above issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
SCCH 5 ::ORDER::
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,26,640/ (Rupees Twenty Five Lakhs Twenty Six Thousand Six Hundred Forty Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation at the ratio of 50:30:20 in the award amount.
